summary.title: Best practices for writing code comments
summary.one_liner: Nine rules for writing comments that help readers, such as avoiding comments that duplicate code, explaining unidiomatic code, linking to sources, and marking TODOs.
keywords: code tells you how comments tell you why
takeaways: Do not write comments that restate the code; they add clutter and go out of date.
Rewrite unclear code with better names instead of relying on comments to explain it.
Explain unidiomatic or non-obvious code, and link to the original source of copied code.
Add comments when fixing bugs and mark known incomplete work with TODO comments, ideally linked to an issue.
summary.summary: The article, published on the Stack Overflow blog, argues that comments are hard to measure for quality and that bad comments are worse than none. It presents nine rules with code examples drawn from real projects, such as Unix source, App Inventor, and Kotlin code. The rules cover avoiding redundant comments, not using comments to excuse unclear code, explaining idioms that look odd, citing sources and references, documenting bug fixes, and flagging incomplete implementations with TODOs. It concludes that comments complement good code by explaining why, while code explains how.
